Motor seed-to-voxel

All-atlas motor seed-to-voxel analysis

Walking intervention · functional connectivity with TFCE · bidirectional Granger pilot · cortical, subcortical and cerebellar seeds

612planned seeds
9atlases
45new-analysis subjects
8pilot seeds
Study context versus analysis cohort. The established longitudinal FC feature table contains 54 subjects (29 Control / 25 Walking) / 107 sessions; the planning record excludes 13 single-session subjects from that study cohort. This new seed-to-voxel analysis uses a separately frozen, stricter cohort of 45 subjects (26 Control / 19 Walking) / 90 sessions with mean FD ≤ 0.3 and both XCP-D sessions available. These cohorts are not interchangeable.

Analysis status

All-atlas FC–TFCE: partial (589/612 seeds with complete outputs)
Bidirectional Granger pilot: complete (8/8 seeds with complete outputs)
FC-preprocessed Granger sensitivity: complete (8/8 seeds with complete outputs)

No new result is implied by this report shell. A section is populated only when its stats table exists. Legacy Motor L/R results are shown as historical context, not as substitutes for the 612-seed analysis or the eight-seed voxelwise Granger pilot.

Scope and interpretation

The seed set includes all validated cortical motor selections from the nine rendered atlases, plus every subcortical and cerebellar parcel in the integrated atlases. Extended-system parcels are not asserted to be exclusively motor. Overlapping atlases are sensitivity representations, not independent replications.

Multiplicity. Randomise TFCE controls the voxelwise maximum-statistic error rate within each seed/contrast map. It does not jointly correct across seeds, atlases, EC directions or contrasts. All-family findings therefore require cautious, atlas-stratified interpretation and separate across-seed validation.

Is seed-to-voxel effective connectivity possible?

Yes, as an exploratory directed-connectivity estimate. The pilot uses bivariate lag-1 Granger F-statistics in both directions on unsmoothed EC-variant BOLD. At TR = 0.8 s, regional haemodynamic latency and preprocessing can produce directed effects; these maps are hypothesis-generating and non-causal. Unrestricted DCM to every voxel is not a practical substitute; sDCM requires a smaller prespecified network and explicit models.

Seed definitions

All rows come from derivatives/analysis/261108-motor-seed-voxel/manifest/motor_seed_manifest.tsv. Extended subcortical/cerebellar inclusion is explicit; it does not imply motor-only function.

Seed-to-voxel functional connectivity

Primary design: XCP-D denoised/smoothed BOLD → ROI mean timeseries → Pearson correlation → Fisher-z → subject post−pre delta → two-sample Walking versus Control randomise TFCE. The new analysis uses 45 subjects (26 Control / 19 Walking), with exact subject order stored beside every delta stack.

Other existing motor products

Individual Schaefer-200/4S256 SomMot maps and older 5,000-permutation TFCE outputs exist, but their 39-subject cohort includes sessions excluded by later corrections. Older Welch/GRF findings are parametric sensitivity results, not TFCE evidence. They are not silently reused as new 45-subject results.

Directed effective connectivity — Granger pilot

Hypothesis-generating and non-causal. Bivariate Granger maps at TR = 0.8 s are sensitive to haemodynamic latency, filtering, noise and region-specific response shapes. “Out” means seed→voxel and “in” means voxel→seed; neither establishes biological causation.

The pilot includes eight cortical, subcortical and cerebellar seeds from the manifest. It uses unsmoothed EC-variant BOLD, bivariate lag-1 VAR models, log(1+F), separate out/in maps, subject deltas and the same two-sample TFCE framework. Exact permutation counts are recorded in the result table.

Full-scope extraction progress

Each variant has 810 atlas–session tasks (9 atlases × 90 sessions). An atlas is ready for group randomise only after all 90 sessions are complete for every seed in that atlas.

Why not whole-brain DCM for every seed?

DCM/sDCM requires a biologically specified network and model space. Repeating an unrestricted model from every seed to every voxel would be computationally and inferentially unwieldy and would not solve haemodynamic non-identifiability. A later sDCM stage should use a small prespecified motor network and independent or split-data node/model selection.

Methods, reproducibility and sensitivity

Cohort freezing

The new FC and EC cohort tables each contain 45 subjects / 90 sessions (26 Control / 19 Walking), selected from Control/Walking participants with two sessions, mean FD ≤ 0.3 and the required XCP-D files. Subjects 056 and 057 remain excluded because of the documented session-data problems. Exact files and subject order are in manifest/cohort_fc.tsv and manifest/cohort_ec.tsv.

Functional connectivity

  1. Use XCP-D denoised BOLD without re-including motion, aCompCor or other confound regressors.
  2. Average each integer-label ROI; compute Pearson seed-to-voxel correlation and Fisher-z.
  3. Apply the dilated MNI brain mask.
  4. Compute ses-02 − ses-01 per subject.
  5. Run two-sample Walking versus Control randomise with both contrasts and TFCE; 5,000 permutations are the full-analysis default. Any pilot with fewer permutations is labelled by its exact table value.
  6. Threshold corrected-p at 0.95, extract clusters, and report peak coordinates plus AAL3, Harvard–Oxford cortical/subcortical, and cerebellar anatomical composition.

TFCE mask

Only voxels inside the dilated MNI brain mask enter the seed correlations and group TFCE tests. Cluster masks are subsequently converted to the FSL MNI152 2 mm grid for anatomical atlas queries.

Directed EC

Both Granger variants use pairwise lag-1 (0.8 s) VAR models on the same 45-subject cohort: unsmoothed EC-minimal BOLD in ec/ and denoised/smoothed FC-preprocessed BOLD in ec_fc_sensitivity/. The vectorized implementation is tested against statsmodels in both directions. Constant/non-finite voxels are background. Both variants are exploratory/non-causal, and out/in families are never pooled. Seed voxels remain in the target maps, but within-seed/self effects are excluded from interpretation.

Atlas spaces and labels

Integer atlases use nearest-neighbour interpolation. DiFuMo-256 remains native MNI152NLin2009cAsym for QC but is transformed to the MNI152NLin6Asym BOLD grid for analysis using the TemplateFlow nonlinear H5 transform and ANTs NearestNeighbor; affine-only substitution is forbidden. All 256 labels must survive. Longevity uses its actual label order: Tian 1–32, Schaefer 33–432, cerebellum 433–442.

Multiplicity and sensitivity

TFCE is within-map correction only. There is no joint correction across 612 seeds, 9 atlases, both EC directions or both contrasts. Results are therefore presented by atlas/system and labelled exploratory at the all-family level. Different atlas solutions overlap substantially and are sensitivity representations rather than independent evidence.

Reproducibility

python script/build_motor_seed_manifest.py
python script/motor_seed_voxel_fc.py --pilot --joint-extraction  # eight-seed FC pilot
python script/motor_seed_voxel_fc.py --joint-extraction          # all 612 FC seeds
python script/motor_seed_voxel_granger.py --stage all        # eight-seed EC pilot
python script/report/render_motor_seed_voxel_figures.py --modality both --pilot
python script/report/prepare_motor_seed_voxel_stats.py
python script/report/build_motor_seed_voxel_report.py
pytest -q tests/e2e/test_motor_seed_voxel_report.py

Source tables live under derivatives/analysis/261108-motor-seed-voxel/{fc,ec,stats}. The HTML builder does not recompute statistical tests.
